briefs.name: Dow
briefs.headline: Dow futures rise 929 points Monday after an 8% weekly drop into a correction
briefs.summary: Markets close Thursday, November 26, for Thanksgiving and shut at 1 p.m. Eastern on Friday, leaving about 3.5 trading days. The Conference Board's consumer confidence report comes Tuesday, November 24, a read on how shoppers feel before the holidays. Selling was worldwide on Friday: Japan's Nikkei fell 5.06% and Germany's DAX 2.6%. Deere, which makes farm and building machines, reports on Wednesday, November 25.
bull: TradingKey named Walmart, UnitedHealth and J&J as defensive picks, and all three are Dow members whose sales tend to hold up when the economy slows.
The 10-year Treasury rate fell 0.14 points on Friday to 4.91%, which makes borrowing a bit cheaper for Dow companies and their customers.
Deutsche Bank strategists said 'a lot of bad news is already being priced,' meaning the worst fears may already be in stock prices.
bear: Futures put about 82% to 90% odds on a quarter-point Fed hike in December, raising loan costs for Dow banks and their customers.
Capital Economics' Thomas Mathews said the US market has further to fall, so the drop may not be over.
The average 30-year mortgage rate hit 7.28%, which makes big purchases like homes costly and can slow spending.

briefs.about: The Dow Jones Industrial Average tracks 30 big, well-known US companies, like Apple, JPMorgan, Walmart and Nvidia. Higher-priced stocks count more, so a few members can move it a lot.
briefs.whyMoved: The Dow fell 4,200.22 points, or 8.02%, last week to 48,147.33 on November 20, about 12% below its high, which counts as a correction. Its 2026 gain shrank to just 0.2% from 13.1% on August 5. The Dow held up a bit better than the Nasdaq's 10% drop because it is only 30 companies and few are chip makers, though member Nvidia fell 14% on Friday alone. The Dow is weighted by share price, so high-priced members like UnitedHealth, which rose 2.84% to $339.85 on Friday, move it more than lower-priced ones like Nvidia at $125.53.

watch.what: Consumer confidence report at 10 a.m. Eastern; a drop would hint shoppers may spend less this holiday season.

October PCE inflation and a second look at third-quarter GDP at 8:30 a.m. Eastern; after October consumer prices rose 0.4% in a month, a cooler reading would ease rate-hike fears and a hotter one would add to them.
Fed rate decision after the Dec 8-9 meeting: futures put about 82% to 90% odds on a quarter-point hike; a bigger hike would likely hurt more, while a calmer message could help.

briefs.name: Russell 2000
briefs.headline: Russell 2000 ends a 7.5% losing week at 2,581 as Thanksgiving week begins
briefs.summary: Early Monday, futures pointed to gains of 2.1% for the S&P 500 and 3.5% for the Nasdaq 100 after the selloff. The average 30-year mortgage rate is 7.28%, which weighs on small builders and lenders. Markets close Thursday for Thanksgiving and shut at 1 p.m. Eastern on Friday. Best Buy reports on Tuesday, November 24, an early hint at how holiday shoppers are spending.
bull: Consumer confidence comes out Tuesday, November 24; small companies mostly sell inside the US, so a steady reading would be good news for them.
The 10-year Treasury rate slipped to 4.91% Friday, near the low end of its 4.91% to 5.15% range for the week, which helps companies that borrow a lot.
Deutsche Bank strategists said 'a lot of bad news is already being priced,' meaning prices may already reflect the worst fears.
bear: Crypto-linked small stocks were crushed last week: miner MARA fell 27.2% and IREN 34.9% as bitcoin dropped about 12%.
The VIX fear gauge closed the week at 35.89, its highest since April 2025, and nervous investors often sell smaller, riskier stocks first.
October consumer prices rose 0.4% in a month, and a hot PCE reading on November 25 could lock in a December rate hike.

briefs.about: The Russell 2000 tracks about 2,000 smaller US companies, such as regional banks, small factories and young health companies. It shows how smaller businesses are doing compared with giants.
briefs.whyMoved: The Russell 2000 fell 208.70 points, or 7.48%, last week to 2,581.79 on November 20, including a 2.76% drop on Friday. That is 15.9% below its August 14 close of 3,068.42, getting closer to the 20% drop that counts as a bear market. Smaller companies fell less than the Nasdaq's 10.02% because few of them are AI chip makers, but they were hurt by rising bets on a December Fed rate hike, now about 82% to 90% likely in futures. Many small companies borrow at loan rates that change, so a hike raises their interest bills faster than for cash-rich giants and can eat into thin profits.

watch.what: Consumer confidence report; a drop would hint US shoppers may pull back, which hurts small companies that sell mostly at home.

October PCE inflation and a second look at third-quarter GDP at 8:30 a.m. Eastern; after October consumer prices rose 0.4% in a month, a cooler reading would ease rate-hike fears and a hotter one would add to them.

briefs.headline: Micron plunges 13.9% to $594.73 after a warning that memory prices are falling
briefs.about: Micron makes memory chips, the parts that store data in computers, phones and the giant data centers that run AI. Its main products are DRAM and NAND flash memory, plus HBM, a fast memory built for AI chips.
briefs.summary: On November 5 Micron fell more than 17% after Bloomberg reported it paused a $4.5 billion memory factory in Taiwan over a labor dispute; Taiwan makes about three-fifths of its regular memory chips. Last quarter Micron earned $33.42 a share, up from $3.03 a year earlier, and it expects about $61.5 billion of sales this quarter. Its board approved $35.16 billion of stock buybacks that can start December 9, though government chip-factory funding rules limit how much it can buy. Micron's next quarterly report is expected in December.
bull: Micron expects about $61.5 billion of sales this quarter, up from $54.2 billion last quarter, so demand for its chips is still growing for now.
Buybacks of up to $35.16 billion can start December 9, which would shrink the number of shares and give each one a bigger slice of profit.
With $73.5 billion of cash and investments against $4.7 billion of debt, Micron can keep building factories even if prices fall for a while.
bear: TrendForce says NAND prices have already dropped 20% and should keep falling in the first half of 2027, which would cut Micron's profit per chip.
Micron has now had two huge one-day drops this month, more than 17% on November 5 and 13.9% on November 20, showing how nervous investors are.
The paused $4.5 billion Taiwan factory matters because Taiwan makes about three-fifths of Micron's regular memory chips.
briefs.nextEvent: Micron's next quarterly report, expected in December 2026

briefs.name: Micron Technology
briefs.whyMoved: Micron lost $95.71, or 13.9%, to close at $594.73 on Friday, November 20, and is down 23.6% from $778.31 on November 13. The trigger was a warning from the research firm TrendForce that big Chinese cloud companies will likely order fewer storage drives next year, that NAND memory prices have already dropped 20% in the open market, and that they should keep falling in early 2027; Sandisk fell 14.3% on the same news, and the whole chip group crashed as Nvidia fell 14%. NAND is only about 26% of Micron's sales; the rest is DRAM, but investors fear DRAM prices could slip too. Micron's record profits come from memory prices being very high, so even a small drop in prices cuts deeply into the money it keeps on each chip.

watch.what: Micron's buyback window opens, and the Fed decides on interest rates the same day. Fast buying would show Micron thinks its stock is cheap.
Next quarterly report. Good: sales near the $61.5 billion goal and steady prices. Bad: a weaker outlook as memory prices fall.

briefs.headline: Domino's gets an upgrade to a $400 target, but US store sales grew just 0.3%
briefs.about: Domino's Pizza is the world's biggest pizza delivery chain. Most of its stores are run by franchise owners, who pay Domino's fees and buy dough, cheese and other supplies from it.
briefs.whyMoved: Domino's rose about 2.5% on the morning of November 13 after the research firm Baird upgraded it to 'outperform' and raised its target to $400 from $320, about 20% above the prior day's close. Baird sees a 'clearer path' to better sales because the average order size grew in the third quarter and Domino's is shortening its discount deals and adding menu items people add on. The rest of the two weeks was quiet, and the stock is still down more than 18% in 2026. Domino's makes most of its money from fees franchise owners pay on their sales and from selling them supplies, so its profit depends on sales at existing stores, which grew only 0.3% in the US last quarter.
briefs.summary: Third-quarter revenue was $1.19 billion and profit was $4.60 a share, both above what analysts expected. Global retail sales rose 3.2% to $4.84 billion, slower than 6.3% a year earlier, and international same-store sales rose just 0.2%. On October 30 Domino's lowered its 2026 goal for new US stores and for operating profit growth, citing pressure on franchise owners' profits. BMO Capital also rates Domino's 'outperform' with a $390 target, while 16 of 30 analysts say hold.
bull: Baird's November 13 upgrade to a $400 target points to bigger average orders, which matter because more money per order helps both Domino's and its franchise owners.
Profit per share rose to $4.60 from $4.08 a year earlier, even though US store sales barely grew.
13 of 30 analysts rate Domino's a buy and only 1 says sell, with targets as high as $425.
bear: US same-store sales grew only 0.3% last quarter, down from 5.2% a year earlier, and the CFO expects 2026 growth at the low end of low single digits.
Domino's cut its 2026 goal for new US stores on October 30, and Baird warns weaker 2026 results will likely slow store openings in 2027 too.
Markets expect a Fed rate hike at the December 8-9 meeting, and higher rates make it costlier for franchise owners to borrow money to open stores.

watch.what: Fed rate decision. A hike is expected; more hikes would raise franchise owners' borrowing costs and could slow new store openings.

briefs.nextEvent: Fed interest rate decision on December 9, 2026

Nvidia sank about 14% after Reuters reported the SEC is looking into its accounting, and Broadcom fell 12% on a report Google will buy fewer of its chips. The Dow fell less as Walmart and UnitedHealth rose, while smaller Russell 2000 companies slid on fears of a Fed rate hike on December 9.
